mechanicTruth: Uneven tread wear has a shape that points at a cause: wear concentrated down the center tracks with too much air, wear on both outer edges with too little, wear on one edge or a feathered saw-tooth edge with alignment, and evenly spaced scalloped dips (cupping) with a worn shock or strut.

storyboardBeats.narration: Tire wear has a shape. The shape is a clue.
storyboardBeats.onScreenText: WORN DOWN THE MIDDLE MEANS TOO MUCH AIR

storyboardBeats.narration: Worn down the center often means too much air.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Split macro comparison of two tire treads mounted on a rotation stand, no hands, even studio lighting, slow lateral pan from a center-worn tread to an edge-worn tread, 9:16 vertical framing

storyboardBeats.narration: Worn on both edges, too little.

storyboardBeats.narration: One edge, or feathered, points at alignment.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Macro shot of a tire tread showing cupping (scalloped dip wear), camera slowly orbiting the tire surface, dramatic rim light catching the shadow inside each scallop, 9:16 vertical framing

storyboardBeats.narration: Scalloped dips point at a shock or strut.
